title: Two-thirds of open-alert countries have no matching entry in the preserved 2026 funding-plan register
statement: The 100 open GDACS alert episodes in foreknown/registry.json touch 75 distinct iso3 countries. The OCHA/FTS response-plan list preserved the same night (foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-08/fts-plans-2026.json, 35 plans) covers only 25 of those 75 (33%) by iso3 match; 50 countries appear in an open alert episode but not in any preserved 2026 plan. Of those 50, 27 belong to a single pan-European drought episode (gdacs-dr-1018332, which lists 28 iso3 codes and only Ukraine among them has a matching plan). The remaining 23 unmatched countries are a mixed set spanning large or high-income states whose hazards (China/Japan/USA/Russia earthquakes and floods, Canada/Bermuda/Guam/Jamaica cyclones, Greece/Portugal/Tunisia wildfires) are covered by GDACS but absent from this OCHA plan list. This is a statement about what the two committed registers do and do not share tonight, not a claim about funding adequacy or need — the FTS plan list is scoped to humanitarian appeals and was never expected to cover every GDACS-tracked hazard.
method: Built the iso3 set of foreknown/registry.json OPEN futures, and the iso3 set from every plan's `locations[].iso3` in foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-08/fts-plans-2026.json (`data` array), then took the set difference.
worth_watching_because: This is the first night both registers exist together, so the 25/75 overlap is a baseline, not yet a trend. It sets up a per-future signal (see sensor proposal sensor-fts-country-coverage.json) that a later discovery pass or promotion decision can test against subsequent nights.
